caption_used: Mean absolute values of hidden states across model layers, comparing pre-gating, post-gating, and baseline configurations. The hidden state mean before gate (blue dashed line, avg 0.71) remains near zero through approximately layer 15, then rises sharply to a peak of roughly 2.8 at layer 23. The post-gating hidden state mean (orange dotted, avg 0.05) and baseline mean (green solid, avg 0.04) both remain close to zero throughout, with the baseline showing marginally higher values than the post-gating mean in the final layers. The dramatic pre-gating increase beginning at layer 12 demonstrates that gating effectively suppresses the activation amplification observed in deeper layers.

The x-axis is labeled "Layer" and represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 24, with tick marks and labels at integer values. The y-axis is labeled "Abs Mean" and represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 4, with tick marks at integer values.

There are three data series presented as lines. The first is a blue dashed line labeled "hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71". This line begins at approximately 0.1 at layer 0, fluctuates between approximately 0.1 and 0.3 until layer 15, then increases steadily to approximately 1.4 at layer 18, and rises sharply to approximately 2.8 at layer 23, before reaching approximately 3.4 at layer 24. The second is an orange dotted line labeled "hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05". This line remains close to zero, fluctuating between approximately 0.02 and 0.08 across all layers. The third is a green solid line labeled "hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04". This line also remains close to zero, fluctuating between approximately 0.02 and 0.06 across all layers, with slightly higher values than the orange dotted line in the final layers.
